details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:334-340 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Successful fallback hydration leaves _linked_metadata_collection_status as unresolved, causing complete linked-issue metadata to be replaced with an unresolved sentinel.
  WHY: Downstream commit producers refuse the sentinel and stall editor, judge-fix, prepare, and conflict-resolve commits; severity ranges from MAJOR to BLOCKER, using the highest.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5768-5772, 5799-5801, 5964/5978, 6050-6053 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: State reconciliation matches a current provenance-keyed finding to a legacy keyless row solely by model-generated finding_id.
  WHY: A reused finding ID can attach a distinct finding to a footer-less legacy issue, bypassing generated-advisory exact-file enforcement and potentially poisoning later deduplication.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5789-5796 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Remote advisory reconciliation compares raw issue bodies against LF-only startswith/endswith literals without normalizing CRLF.
  WHY: An existing advisory with CRLF line endings is not matched after a lost state write, so reconciliation files a duplicate; severity ranges from NIT to MAJOR, using the highest and noting the disagreement.
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:295 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: closingIssuesReferences(first:50) does not request or handle pagination.
  WHY: A generated advisory after the first 50 closing issues can be omitted, making review_advisory_count zero and skipping the exact-file scope guard; severity ranges from NIT to MAJOR, using the highest and noting the disagreement.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5834, 5857, 5792 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: prose() strips backticks from finding_id before writing the advisory marker, while reconciliation compares the original finding_id.
  WHY: A finding_id containing backticks can never match its generated remote marker, preventing remote re-adoption after creation.
- scripts/minimax_minimax-m3 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Verified-empty linked-issue metadata can produce an empty artifact rather than a valid empty array.
  WHY: review_commit_changes.sh rejects the resulting malformed metadata and aborts legitimate commits.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5784-5787 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The per-tracking-number advisory search cache is not invalidated after filing and can retain stale rows for later reconciliation.
  WHY: A later advisory can use a stale legacy finding_id fallback and adopt an issue whose new provenance key was never recorded.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5749-5761 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A legacy backlog row with an invalid or short head_sha repeatedly fails legacy-key derivation without recording a terminal failure.
  WHY: The row remains queued indefinitely, repeatedly consumes the per-tick attempt cap, and delays project completion.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5758 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Legacy-key derivation includes head_sha, so the same finding can receive different keys when integration-branch heads change.
  WHY: Reprocessing an in-flight finding after a head change can respawn the same advisory instead of deduplicating it.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:207-237; scripts/security_audit.sh:1377-1382, 1392, 1441-1443 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The scope guard and security_audit.sh apply inconsistent normalization and rejection rules to cited paths.
  WHY: A path such as ./\* can pass orchestrator scope validation but be rejected by the audit engine, leaving inconsistent audit and security-pass state.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1505, 1540-1566, 1575-1621 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Causal-diff caching still materializes and reparses an entire potentially huge cross-file diff.
  WHY: Large project ranges can exhaust the codex-cli budget before the security-audit step reaches the LLM.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5777-5778 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: legacy_advisory_marker is computed but is not used by the new jq authorization filter.
  WHY: The identifier is dead state and creates misleading marker-handling behavior.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2521-2545; scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:280-304 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Generated-advisory conflict guards evaluate all paths in git diff --cached during a merge rather than only resolver-owned changes.
  WHY: Cleanly auto-merged base-branch changes outside the cited file cause the guard to reject otherwise valid conflict-resolution commits.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2022-2027, 2037-2061; scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:451 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: git add -u can stage unrelated tracked workspace changes before the generated-advisory exact-file guard evaluates the staged set.
  WHY: A routinely dirty .ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt or other unrelated file can make judge-fix and fallback editor commits fail.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)
